evidenceAudit.scope: Adults in primary care: cardiovascular risk assessment, lipid testing, statin treatment for primary and secondary prevention, lipid targets, escalation (ezetimibe, PCSK9-targeted therapy) and monitoring. Verified against NICE NG238 (December 2023); doses and contraindications from US FDA prescribing information. QRISK3 is validated in the UK population and may misestimate risk in Saudi patients. A Saudi national lipid guideline was not reviewed for this version. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.

pathophysiology.summary: Atherosclerosis is driven by apolipoprotein-B–containing lipoproteins (mainly LDL) entering the arterial wall, where they are oxidised and taken up by macrophages to form foam cells and plaque. The higher the LDL (or non-HDL) cholesterol and the longer the exposure, the greater the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke and peripheral arterial disease.
keyMechanisms: Non-HDL cholesterol (total minus HDL) captures all atherogenic particles, including triglyceride-rich remnants.
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation → 30–50%+ LDL reduction and fewer CVD events.
Ezetimibe blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption (NPC1L1); PCSK9 inhibitors increase LDL-receptor recycling.
Secondary causes: hypothyroidism, diabetes, nephrotic syndrome, CKD, cholestatic liver disease, alcohol, drugs (steroids, antipsychotics).
Familial hypercholesterolaemia: inherited, very high LDL from birth, premature CHD.

symptoms: Usually asymptomatic until a cardiovascular event.
Family history of premature CHD (first-degree relative, men under 55, women under 65).
physicalSigns: Tendon xanthomas, xanthelasma, corneal arcus under 45 (familial hypercholesterolaemia).
Eruptive xanthomas, lipaemia retinalis (very high triglycerides).
Signs of established CVD: carotid bruit, absent pulses.
redFlags: Total cholesterol above 9.0 mmol/L or non-HDL above 7.5 mmol/L — specialist assessment (NICE)
Triglycerides above 20 mmol/L (not due to alcohol or poor diabetes control) — urgent specialist review for pancreatitis risk
Unexplained muscle symptoms on a statin with CK above 5× ULN
Pregnancy or planning pregnancy on a statin
precipitants: Diet high in saturated fat; obesity; inactivity

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Very high LDL, xanthomas, family history — use the FH pathway (NICE CG71).
Hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, poorly controlled diabetes, drugs.
High triglycerides from obesity, alcohol, diabetes.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess risk
actions: Record smoking, alcohol, BP, BMI, full lipids, diabetes status, renal function, transaminases, TSH if symptomatic (NICE 1.5.5).
Use QRISK3 for people 25–84 without CVD; type 1 diabetes, CKD and FH are high risk without scoring.
Exclude familial hypercholesterolaemia and secondary causes.

clinicalManagement.title: Primary prevention
actions: Optimise lifestyle and other risk factors first; offer statin if lifestyle change is ineffective or inappropriate.
QRISK3 10% or more: atorvastatin 20 mg once daily; consider even below 10% if the person prefers or risk is underestimated.
Type 1 diabetes: offer atorvastatin 20 mg if older than 40, diabetes for more than 10 years, nephropathy or other risk factors.
Target: more than 40% reduction in non-HDL cholesterol; if not met check adherence and consider increasing the dose.

clinicalManagement.title: Secondary prevention (established CVD)
actions: Atorvastatin 80 mg whatever the cholesterol, unless interactions, high adverse-effect risk or preference (then lower dose).
ACS: start in hospital; full lipids on admission and at 2–3 months.
Target LDL 2.0 mmol/L or less or non-HDL 2.6 mmol/L or less.
Not at target on maximum tolerated statin: add ezetimibe; then PCSK9-targeted therapy (alirocumab, evolocumab) or inclisiran per eligibility. Ezetimibe may be added even if at target.

clinicalManagement.title: Chronic kidney disease
actions: Atorvastatin 20 mg for primary or secondary prevention; increase if target not met and eGFR 30 or more; agree higher doses with a renal specialist if eGFR below 30 (NICE 1.8).

clinicalManagement.title: Statin intolerance
actions: Measure CK; if below 5× ULN reassure and look for other causes; consider a lower dose or alternative statin; restart after interaction-related stops.
Do not routinely use fibrates, nicotinic acid or omega-3 compounds to prevent CVD (NICE 1.12).

clinicalManagement.title: Pregnancy
actions: Statins are contraindicated in pregnancy: stop 3 months before trying to conceive and do not restart until breastfeeding has finished (NICE).

monitoring: Lipids and ALT at 2–3 months; ALT at 12 months
contraindications: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis
